title: Draft 2023–2026 strategic plan reviewed
subtitle: Leisure fee assistance policy changes, Laurel Creek Trail funding, a sustainability update and a senior staff farewell.
overview: Council reviewed the draft 2023–2026 Strategic Plan, including its proposed vision, mission, guiding principles and five strategic priorities. Council received the report as information {{vote:m3}}, and staff will take feedback, open until May 29, and report back with a final plan. Councillors raised wording, housing, infrastructure, transportation and accountability, and a community delegate asked for explicit inclusion of anti-Palestinian racism.

Council also approved changes to the Fee Assistance Leisure Access Program Policy {{vote:m4}}. It released $106,000 in 2023 capital funding for the Laurel Creek Trail around the Conservation Area {{vote:m5}}. Staff said the trail will be built in phases and that winter maintenance will be considered through the ongoing sidewalk and winter control review.

Council heard an update from Sustainable Waterloo Region and met in closed session earlier in the afternoon. The minutes report no decisions from that session. The meeting also marked the final council meeting of a senior city staff member.

decisions.item: 2019–2022 Strategic Plan close-out and draft 2023–2026 plan
decisions.detail: Council received the report as information, with feedback on the draft plan open until May 29 and staff to report back on the final plan {{vote:m3}}.
Council approved report COM2023-010 and the changes to the Fee Assistance Leisure Access Program Policy (M-008) {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved releasing $106,000 in 2023 capital funding, already approved in the 2023 Capital Budget, for the Laurel Creek Trail around the Conservation Area {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Vision wording: some councillors found sustainability and future-ready overlapping and suggested shortening the vision to a future-ready community for all. Others wanted climate action kept explicit, and one said stability and infrastructure should not be lost.

Mission wording: several councillors questioned whether 'actively respond' was too passive and suggested bolder or more collaborative language. One suggested 'diverse communities' in place of 'our diverse community', and another asked whether 'our' implied ownership.

Housing and priorities: some councillors were surprised affordability and housing did not appear more prominently, given the engagement results. Others preferred 'diverse housing options' as something the City can influence. Some wanted infrastructure and transportation split, with Vision Zero given more weight.

A delegate supported the plan's direction and asked that the equity objectives name all ethnic and cultural communities, address visibility, and list anti-Palestinian racism. Staff said they would look at how to incorporate the recommendations.

On the accountability of the plan, staff said performance indicators will come with the final plan. They said they would keep the number manageable and use business plans and ongoing community conversations. On the trail, staff said winter maintenance would be phased and considered in the sidewalk and winter control review.
